title: Giving advice before a shot
question: If one golfer asks another, 'Which club should I use?' and gets an answer, what is the penalty?

choices.text: Both the player asking and the one answering get 2 penalty strokes.
The player who asks for or receives advice, and the one who gives it, each get 2 penalty strokes.
Only the person giving advice gets a penalty.

explanation: If a player asks for or gives advice about how to play a shot (such as club selection), both the player who asks/receives and the one giving advice get a two-stroke penalty in stroke play.

juniorVersion.title: Talking about which club to use
juniorVersion.question: If one golfer asks another, 'Which club should I use?' and the other answers, what happens?

choices.text: Nothing happens, you can always do this.
Both the golfer who asks and the one who answers get 2 extra shots added.
The golfer who asks or gets help, and the one who gives help, both get 2 extra shots added.
Only the person who gives help gets a penalty.

juniorVersion.explanation: If someone asks what club to use and the other answers, both golfers get 2 extra shots added to their score. You are not allowed to help pick clubs during a round.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The stick you use to hit the golf ball.
An extra shot added to your score for breaking a rule.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind young golfers that you have to make your own choices on the course. No giving or getting help with choosing clubs during the round!
likelyMisconceptions: They might think it's always okay to talk about which club to use.
They might think only the person giving advice gets a penalty.
